pages.text: All six cultivated tobacco varieties use the same basic crop rules. Plant tobacco seeds on $(item)farmland$(). Natural growth requires local raw brightness of at least $(item)9$(). Bonemeal can advance the lower half of a plant until the crop is mature.

Tobacco has stages $(item)0 through 7$(). Stages 0–3 occupy one block. From stage 4 onward the plant becomes two blocks tall, with the upper half carrying the later growth stage. Stage 7 is fully mature.
pages.title: Growth Stages

pages.text: Breaking mature tall tobacco yields raw leaves and seeds. Harvest timing matters to growth quality: fully mature is best, one stage early is penalized, and earlier harvesting is heavily penalized. If quality matters, wait for Stage 7.
pages.title: Harvesting

pages.text: Sneak-right-click a growing tobacco plant for a short qualitative message even without Spectacles. For exact growth percentage, environment rating, and potential-quality range, wear Tobacconist's Spectacles.
